findings.issue: The note says 'In 519 a bishop who accepted Chalcedon expelled the monks who refused it.' The date is wrong. The Chronicle's section 89 has the patrician arrive in Seleucid 831 (519/20) to remove Paul. Paul left on 27 Tammuz 833 (July 522), and Asclepius entered Edessa on 23 Tishri I 834 (October 522). Section 90 dates the expulsion to 24 Canun I (December), 'after the entering of Asclepius'. That is December 522, not 519. The locus label 'Chron. Edessa 90 (An. 831 = 519)' carries the same error. The drafter asked for the conversion to be checked; it fails. This is a factual error stated as fact in public text.
findings.evidence: cic/texts/chronicle-of-edessa_cowper.txt line 223 (sections 89-90, read in full): 'came the patrician ... in An. 831 ... Paul departed from Edessa on Tammuz (July) 27, of the year 833, and Asclepius ... entered Edessa on the 23rd of Tishrin the former (October), of the year 834 ... 90. And in the month Canun the former (December), on the 24th in it, after the entering of Asclepius the bishop to Edessa, he expelled the Oriental monks'.
findings.fix: Change the note to 'In 522 a bishop who accepted Chalcedon expelled the monks who refused it.' Change the locus to 'Chron. Edessa 90 (An. 834 = 522)'. Optionally add the section 89 sentence on Paul, the anti-Chalcedonian bishop removed in 519-522, as a second quote; it shows the see itself in the anti-Chalcedonian camp.

findings.issue: The link claims 'continued as', which means the same community or see. Its last sentence and its secondary make a different claim: 'Historians treat that church as a daughter of Edessa's Christianity.' A daughter is 'gave rise to', not 'continued as'. Wigram pp. 25-26 says exactly that: Persia received the gospel from Edessene teachers, and the 'Church of the Easterns' was Edessa's 'daughter'. He says nothing about the see of Nisibis passing in 363. The 'Historians treat' phrasing also turns one 1910 author into a consensus. The Barhadbeshabba quote does not show 'its church passed with it' either. It shows Ephrem leaving Nisibis for Edessa when the city was handed to Persia. What actually shows continuity of the see is the 410 signature and the metropolitan list (Osee of Nisibis).
findings.evidence: cic/texts/wigram_introduction-to-the-history-of-the-assyrian-church-100-640_1910.txt lines 1274-1310 (pp. 25-26: 'received the gospel from teachers whose head-quarters were at Edessa'; 'nursing mother'; 'The Church of the Easterns was the daughter, not of Antioch, but of Edessa'). cic/texts/barhadbeshabba_cause-de-la-fondation-des-ecoles-po4-syr-fra_scher1908.txt 20437-20438 (Ephrem 'se retira à Édesse'). cic/texts/synodicon-orientale_recueil-de-synodes-nestoriens-syr-fra_chabot1902.txt 17745-17746, 17861.
findings.fix: Keep 'continued as', since it mirrors the census continuesAs pairing and the see evidence fits that type. Make the note claim only see continuity. For example: 'Nisibis passed to Persia in 363. At the Persian church's synod of 410, its bishop Osee signed the acts and was named second metropolitan.' Drop the 'daughter' sentence and drop Wigram from this link. Replace the Barhadbeshabba quote, or keep it only for the handover of the city. If a vendored line names a pre-363 bishop of Nisibis (Jacob), add it; the link then shows the see on both sides and can be graded Documented. Without it, the link can stay at a grade below Documented, which needs no secondary for the inference. If the 'daughter' relationship is wanted, it belongs on a separate 'gave rise to' link carrying Wigram.

findings.issue: The link is graded Widely Accepted on Wigram pp. 25-26. That page says the Edessene church 'was merged in that ecclesiastical circle that developed into the Patriarchate of Antioch'. It does not name the Syriac Orthodox church or the anti-Chalcedonian split. Its subject is the Persian church, and its claim is the general Antiochene orbit, which both Chalcedonian and anti-Chalcedonian heirs share. The method says Widely Accepted needs a secondary work for the consensus reading itself. The drafter's own flag concedes Wigram supports the line 'in general, not the Syriac Orthodox by name'. findings.issue: The note says Jerome wrote 'that Origen should be read for his learning, just as we read Tertullian'.
